audit_findings.title: Growth may rely on acquisitions whose purchase cost is excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $92.404 million of stated acquisition consideration in 2023-2024 ($87.671 million of net acquisition cash outflows), versus a $25.2 million OE increase from 2022 to 2025; forecast valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical acquired earnings enter the OE anchor and growth history, while acquisition consideration remains outside ordinary capital expenditures and the valuation bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: A key element of our growth strategy is to pursue acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisitions and their excluded purchase costs are demonstrated, but the record does not separate organic from acquired OE. Because the base and bull cases capitalize 5%-7% growth and acquisitions are an explicit growth strategy, treating purchased growth as costless is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic OE bridge for 2018-2025 by removing acquired revenue, profit, working capital, and maintenance capital expenditure. Rerun every scenario using supportable organic growth or a recurring acquisition-reinvestment allowance.

audit_findings.title: The zero-growth bear case may omit a credible continuing contraction
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 revenue declined $51.778 million or 5.4%, federal revenue declined $76.195 million or 17.2%, operating income declined $3.658 million or 4.7%, and net income declined $3.042 million or 6.0%; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Further revenue loss and operating deleverage would reduce forecast OE below the flat $117.2 million bear-case starting level.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in revenue was driven by a reduction of $279.5 million from our U.S. federal government clients, primarily as a result of terminated contracts in 2025 due to the Administration’s changing priorities and the actions recommended by DOGE, as well as the disruption in the typical U.S. federal government procurement cycle.
audit_findings.explanation: Continuing contraction is more than a hypothetical risk: H1 2026 revenue, operating income, and net income remained below the comparable period. Q2 revenue and operating income were approximately flat year over year, so the record does not prove continued deterioration, but it does make a negative-growth bear path credible and potentially valuation-changing.
audit_findings.action: Compute 2026 trailing-twelve-month OE and reconcile federal awards, funded backlog, terminations, utilization, and realized cost reductions. Rerun the bear case with the resulting downside trajectory rather than a zero-growth floor.

audit_findings.title: Favorable contract-estimate revisions materially support the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.8 million of 2025 operating-income benefit, equal to 12.6% of the $117.2 million OE anchor, and $0.65 of diluted EPS; H1 2026 net-income benefit was $4.3 million versus $11.6 million in H1 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Cumulative catch-up revisions increase reported earnings and may increase OE unless offset by contract-asset, liability, receivable, or cash-flow adjustments; capitalizing an unusually favorable amount would overstate the anchor and growth base.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, the aggregate net changes in estimates on contracts accounted under the percentage-of-completion method reflected increases of $ 14.8 million , $ 12.7 million , and $ 7.9 million , respectively, to “Operating income” on the Company’s consolidated statements of comprehensive income.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting benefit and its material scale are demonstrated. An OE error is not yet demonstrated because the supplied record does not show how the revisions flowed through cash and working capital or what recurring level is sustainable. The sharp year-over-year reduction in the H1 benefit reinforces the normalization concern.
audit_findings.action: Trace the revisions through revenue, contract assets and liabilities, receivables, collections, taxes, and the OE calculation. Rerun the valuation with a documented normalized revision level, including a zero-benefit sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Recorded tax contingencies may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.7 million gross unrecognized tax benefits, about $1.34 per diluted valuation share and 1.34% of the $1.843 billion base equity value, plus unquantified accrued interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Any expected cash settlement already accrued in prior earnings but absent from forecast OE should be deducted as a non-operating claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The unrecognized tax benefits and the related accrued interest are part of other long-term liabilities on the Company’s consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is unresolved because the gross reserve is not an estimate of the eventual cash payment. Nevertheless, even deducting the entire filed gross balance would reduce base value only from $100.14 to about $98.80 per share, still above the $88 reference price; the bear and bull values would similarly fall by about $1.34 per share. Accrued interest is not quantified in the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-reserve roll-forward, accrued interest, expected settlement ranges, and timing. Deduct only the expected net cash settlement not already captured in OE; no broad valuation rerun is needed unless that evidence identifies a substantially larger claim.

audit_findings.title: Unaudited government contract years create latent repayment exposure
audit_findings.mechanism: Disallowed costs, indirect-rate true-ups, repayment demands, penalties, or lost profit could reduce future OE or create a liability requiring an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Federal government audits have been completed on our incurred contract costs only through 2022 and 2023 for our NIH-cognizant indirect rates and through 2015 for our USAID-cognizant indirect rates, but audits for costs incurred on work performed since then have not yet been completed.
audit_findings.explanation: The unaudited periods are demonstrated, but no questioned costs, settlement estimate, excess reserve, or historical loss rate is supplied. The exposure concerns revenue and costs already recognized, so it is not merely forward-looking; however, the record cannot establish whether the amount is material to the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile open audit years by cognizant agency, cost base, recorded reserves, historical settlement percentages, questioned costs, and subsequent audit developments. Rerun OE or the bridge if the resulting expected loss is material.

audit_findings.title: Finance-leased equipment may bypass the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.262 million finance-lease liability at December 31, 2025, falling to $9.920 million at June 30, 2026; $2.040 million annual finance-lease amortization equals 1.7% of anchor OE, and the June liability equals about $0.54 per valuation share or 0.54% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash leased-asset addition can escape investing cash flow while its amortization is added back to OE; deducting neither the asset investment nor equivalent replacement capital expenditure would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we also have finance leases for equipment and furniture with lease payment obligations through 2029 as discussed in “Note 7 - Leases” in the “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting pathway is valid, but the filed scale is small relative to anchor OE and equity value. The 2025 cash-flow statement reports no finance-lease asset additions, while the existing obligation runs only through 2029. Even treating the entire June 2026 liability as an omitted claim would reduce base value by only about $0.54 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify that the OE schedule captures noncash finance-lease additions in every historical year or includes equivalent replacement capital expenditure. Continue monitoring new lease additions; do not deduct principal separately when the associated asset investment has already been charged.
